title: Pickled Red Cabbage
subtitle: Crisp, sharp, malt-pickled, the classic British accompaniment to pork
excerpt: Pickled red cabbage uses malt vinegar and spices. The cabbage is dry-salted overnight, rinsed, then packed raw into vinegar. Ready in 2 weeks. Makes about three 500 ml jars.
sourceNotes: Mrs Beeton (PG #10136); Pam Corbin, Preserves. Dry-salting overnight draws moisture from the cabbage, keeping it crisp. The cabbage is packed raw, cooking would make it soft.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Ready to eat after 2 weeks. Best within 8 weeks — becomes soft after that.

days.label: Salt the cabbage
tasks: Shred and salt the cabbage; leave overnight

days.label: Rinse and jar
tasks: Pack into jars with spiced vinegar

glossaryTerms.definition: Salting vegetables without liquid and leaving them overnight to draw out moisture, keeping the final pickle crisp.

content.text: Pickled red cabbage is packed raw into cold spiced vinegar,  no cooking, no heat. The overnight
removes excess water from the cabbage so it stays properly crisp in the jar rather than going limp. It goes alongside pork pies, cold meats, cheese, and salt beef. Makes about three 500 ml jars.
Toss the shredded cabbage with the salt in a large bowl. Cover and leave overnight in a cool place or the fridge. The salt will draw out a significant amount of water.
Day 1: Make the spiced vinegar and jar
Rinse the cabbage very thoroughly under cold running water to remove the salt. Taste,  it should be only very lightly salty. Shake dry in a colander and press with a clean cloth.

Combine the vinegar, sugar, peppercorns, cloves, and bay leaves in a jug and stir until the sugar dissolves. Pack the cabbage tightly into sterilised jars and pour the spiced vinegar over, making sure the cabbage is fully submerged. Seal immediately.

items.symptom: Cabbage has gone purple-grey rather than staying red-pink
items.cause: Contact with alkaline water or not enough acid.
items.fix: Make sure the vinegar fully covers the cabbage. Add a few drops of lemon juice to the vinegar if your water is very hard.

items.cause: Not rinsed thoroughly enough after the overnight brine.
items.fix: Rinse for several minutes under cold running water and taste before jarring.

items.cause: Normal, pickled red cabbage softens with time.
items.fix: Use within 6 to 8 weeks of making. The texture is crisp in the first 2 to 4 weeks and gradually softens.

items.cause: Jar too loosely packed, or not enough vinegar.
items.fix: Pack the cabbage in firmly and top up with vinegar if needed. All cabbage must be below the surface.

content.text: Ready after 2 weeks. Best within 6 to 8 weeks. Refrigerate once opened.
